summary: 大型特展可以把新观众带进博物馆，也能带动商店、旅游和其他展览。不过高额投入不保证盈利，过度追逐客流还可能损害内容。作者主张兼顾大型特展、常设展与本地观众的需要。
logic: 平衡大型活动与常设展

paragraphs.brief: 自八十年代以来，“阻击者”一词已成为吸引大量群众的壮观、引人注目的博物馆展览的流行词汇。
sentences: Since the 1980s, the term ‘blockbuster’ has become the fashionable word for spectacular, high-profile museum exhibitions that have the ability to attract large crowds.
自八十年代以来，“阻击者”一词已成为吸引大量群众的壮观、引人注目的博物馆展览的流行词汇。
A blockbuster is a ‘large-scale loan exhibition that people who normally don’t go to museums will stand in line for hours to see’ (Eisen 1984).
一个大片片是"大型贷款展览，通常不去博物馆的人会排队数小时看" (Eisen 1984).
Once the museum that created the exhibition has shown it to its local market, it can be offered to other organizations for a fee.
一旦创建展览的博物馆向当地市场展示，可向其他组织收取费用。
This means that you can boost your own door takings and make money from boosting someone else’s door takings.
这表示你可以提高自己的门和赚钱通过提升别人的门。

paragraphs.brief: 如此吸引的游客可能会在博物馆逗留更长的时间。
sentences: While partaking of the excitement of the blockbuster, visitors thus lured are likely to stay longer at the museum.
如此吸引的游客可能会在博物馆逗留更长的时间。

Betty Churcher, when Director of the Australian National Gallery, summed up the new blockbuster creed as follows: ‘The bonus of the blockbuster exhibitions is that people come to see the blockbuster and they stay to look at the permanent collection, so you are getting broader exposure for your collection.’
Betty Churcher在澳大利亚国家美术馆的主任总结了以下新的禁忌信条：“这些禁忌信教展览的红利是人们来参观禁忌信封，他们留下来看永久收藏，这样你就能为自己的收藏获得更广泛的曝光。”

paragraphs.brief: 现在，博物馆管理员是管理者，博物馆主任不再需要艺术学位，但是，如果博物馆要与其他博物馆竞争，举办吸引大量观众的巡回展览，公共关系技能是必不可少的。
sentences: Museums across the UK, USA, Canada and Australia currently operate under a system of plural funding: revenue raised through contributions by federal, state and/or local governments, combined with revenue raised through admission charges and other activities.
目前，联合王国、美国、加拿大和澳大利亚各地的博物馆都在多元化供资制度下运作：通过联邦、州和(或)地方政府捐款筹集的收入，加上通过入场费和其他活动筹集的收入。
Maintaining and increasing visitor levels is thus paramount and involves not only creating or hiring blockbuster exhibitions, but providing regular exhibition changes and innovations.
因此，保持和增加游客人数至关重要，不仅涉及创建或聘用 " 封锁者 " 展览，而且提供定期的展览变革和创新。
In addition, the visiting public have become known as customers rather than visitors, and the skills that are valued in museums to keep the new customers coming through the door have changed.
此外，来访的公众已被称为顾客，而不是游客，博物馆重视的新客户通过大门的技能已经改变。

Curators are now administrators, and being a museum director no longer requires an Arts degree—but public relations skills are essential if the museum is going to compete with other museums to stage travelling exhibitions which draw huge crowds.
现在，博物馆管理员是管理者，博物馆主任不再需要艺术学位，但是，如果博物馆要与其他博物馆竞争，举办吸引大量观众的巡回展览，公共关系技能是必不可少的。

paragraphs.brief: 博物馆、遗产产业、旅游业、盈利和娱乐业的汇合导致了新的 " 博物馆学 "。
sentences: The convergence of museums, the heritage industry, tourism, profit-making and pleasure-giving has resulted in the new ‘museology’.
博物馆、遗产产业、旅游业、盈利和娱乐业的汇合导致了新的 " 博物馆学 "。
This has given rise to much debate about whether it is appropriate to see museums primarily as tourist attractions.
这引起了关于将博物馆主要视为旅游景点是否适当的大量辩论。

In literature from both the UK and USA, the words that are starting to appear in some descriptions of blockbusters are ‘less scholarly’, ‘non-elitist’ and ‘popularist’, while others extol the virtues of encouraging scholars to co-operate on projects, and to provide exhibitions that cater for a broad selection of the community rather than an elite sector.
在英国和美国的文献中，一些封杀者的描述中开始出现的话语是`学术性低 '、`非精英主义 ' 和`民粹主义者 '，而另一些人则赞美鼓励学者在项目上合作的美德，并提供适合社区广泛选择而不是精英阶层的展览。
Whatever commentators may think, managers of museums worldwide are looking for artful ways to blend culture and commerce, and blockbuster exhibitions are at the top of the list.
不管评论家怎么想，世界各地的博物馆管理人员都在寻找将文化和商业混合在一起的艺术方法，最突出的就是封锁式展览。

paragraphs.brief: 但是，在公共机构中持有的封锁者真的创造出盈余来资助其他活动吗？
sentences: But do blockbusters held in public institutions really create a surplus to fund other activities?
但是，在公共机构中持有的封锁者真的创造出盈余来资助其他活动吗？
If the bottom line is profit, then according to the records of many major museums blockbusters do make money.
如果底线是利润，那么根据许多大博物馆的纪录，破坏者确实赚钱。
For museums in some countries, it may be the money that they require to replace parts of their collections or to fix buildings that are in need of attention.
对于一些国家的博物馆来说，它们可能需要钱来更换其收藏的部分或修复需要注意的建筑物。
For some museums in Australia, it may be the opportunity to illustrate that they are attempting to pay their way by recovering part of their operating costs.
对于澳大利亚的一些博物馆来说，这或许是说明它们试图通过收回其部分运营费用来支付其费用的机会。

Also, creating or hiring a blockbuster has many positive spin-offs: blockbusters mean crowds, and crowds are good for the local economy, providing increased trade for shops, hotels, restaurants, the transport industry and retailers.
此外，创建或雇用一个“封锁者”具有许多积极的附带利益：“封锁者”，意味着人群，人群有利于当地经济，为商店、旅馆、餐馆、运输业和零售商提供了更多的贸易。
The argument that the arts provide sustained economic benefits has been well illustrated in impact studies in the USA and UK.
美英的影响研究充分说明了艺术提供持续经济利益的论点。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，封锁者需要大量资本支出，并需要利用一个组织所有分支机构的资源，而费用并没有到此为止。
sentences: However, blockbusters require large capital expenditure and draw on resources across all branches of an organization, and the costs don’t end there.
然而，封锁者需要大量资本支出，并需要利用一个组织所有分支机构的资源，而费用并没有到此为止。
There is a Human Resource Management cost in addition to a measurable ‘real’ dollar cost.
除了可衡量的 " 实际美元 " 费用之外，还有人力资源管理费用。
Receiving a touring exhibition draws resources from across functional management structures in a project-management style.
接受巡回展览时，会以项目管理方式从各职能管理结构中抽取资源。
Everyone—from general labourers to building services, front-of-house, technical, promotional, educational and administrative staff—is required to perform additional tasks.
从一般劳工到建筑服务、门前服务、技术、宣传、教育和行政人员，每个人都需要承担额外任务。

Furthermore, as an increasing number of institutions try their hand at increasing visitor numbers and memberships (and therefore revenue) by staging blockbuster exhibitions, it may be less likely that blockbusters will continue to provide a surplus to subsidize other activities due to the competitive nature of the market.
此外，随着越来越多的机构试图通过举办阻击性展览来增加游客人数和成员(从而增加收入)，由于市场的竞争性质，阻击者可能不太可能继续提供盈余来补贴其他活动。

paragraphs.brief: 第二，正如一些分析家所争论的那样，" 商店 " 的心态和成本效益分析，以及完全集中于底线，可以将物质挤出展览。
sentences: It has been illustrated in both the UK and USA that the blockbuster ideology has resulted in the false expectation that the momentum required to stage blockbusters can be maintained continually.
英国和美国都表明，这种封锁意识形态导致人们错误地期望能够持续地保持制造封锁者所需的势头。
Creating, mounting or hiring blockbusters is exhausting, with the real costs throughout an institution difficult to calculate.
创建、增加或雇用 " 封锁者 " 已经是累赘，整个机构的实际成本难以计算。
Secondly, as some analysts have argued, the ‘shopkeeping’ mentality and cost-benefit analysis, and a pure concentration on the bottom line, can squeeze substance out of an exhibition.
第二，正如一些分析家所争论的那样，" 商店 " 的心态和成本效益分析，以及完全集中于底线，可以将物质挤出展览。
Taking out substance can be a recipe for blockbuster failure and therefore financial failure.
采取实质性措施可能是造成挫折性失败，从而造成财政失败的诱因。

paragraphs.brief: 也许最好的方法就是平衡混混和定期展览
sentences: Perhaps the best pathway to take is one that balances both blockbusters and regular exhibitions.
也许最好的方法就是平衡混混和定期展览
However, this easy middle ground may only work if you have enough space, and have alternative sources of funding to continue to support the regular, less exciting fare.
但是，这种容易的中间地带只有在有足够的空间，并且有其他资金来源来继续支助正常的、不那么令人兴奋的票价的情况下才能发挥作用。
Perhaps the advice should be to make sure that you find out what your local community wants from you and make sure that your regular activities and exhibitions are more enduring.
也许建议应该是确保你了解你的当地社区想要你做什么，并确保你的日常活动和展览更加持久。

items.en: the reason why museum directors need to constantly alter and update their exhibits
items.zh: 博物馆馆长需要不断改变和更新展品的原因
items.why: 题干问“馆长为何需要不断改变和更新展品”,句中直接指出为保持/增加观众人数，必须定期更换与创新展览。

items.en: mention of the length of time people will queue to see a blockbuster
items.zh: 提到人们排队看一个混球的时间长度
items.why: 题干提 "排队的时间长度",这里明确说“排上几个小时”。

items.en: terms that people have used when referring to blockbusters
items.zh: 人们在提到 " 阻击者 " 时使用的术语
items.why: 题干问“人们用来称呼/形容 blockbusters 的词语",第D段列举了多个词。

items.en: the various ways that institutions like museums get financial support
items.zh: 博物馆等机构获得财政支持的各种方式
items.why: 问“博物馆等机构获得财政支持的各种方式”,此句直接列出多种资金来源。

items.en: These days, museum visitors tend to be referred to as ________.
items.zh: 如今，博物馆往往把参观者称为________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“此外，来访的公众已被称为顾客，而不是游客，博物馆重视的新客户通过大门的技能已经改变”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Museum curators now need ________ rather than academic qualifications.
items.zh: 如今，博物馆策展人需要具备________，只靠学历已不够。
items.why: 问“需要什么而非学术资格”,句中给出必需的“public relations skills”. (尽管主语是director/curator,语义上对应题干。)

items.en: The linking of a range of public institutions that entertain the public is known as ________.
items.zh: 把各种为公众提供娱乐的公共机构联系起来，这种做法称为________。
items.why: 题干描述“把多种公众娱乐机构联系在一起的概念，原文说这种融合产生了“museology”。

items.en: There is discussion about whether museums can be regarded in the same way as other ________.
items.zh: 博物馆能否与其他________同等看待，人们对此还有争论。
items.why: 问“是否能把博物馆看作与其他什么相同”,原文即“tourist attractions”.

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填三个词。

items.en: Which TWO of the following are mentioned by the writer as advantages of blockbusters?
items.zh: 作者提到以下哪两件东西成为了阻击者的优势？
correct: Some of the money they raise can be used for structural repairs.
他们筹集的一些资金可用于结构维修。
Local services benefit from the extra business they bring about.
当地服务机构受益于它们带来的额外业务。

items.en: Which THREE of the following are mentioned by the writer as disadvantages of blockbusters?
items.zh: 作者提到以下哪些三者是阻击者的劣势？
correct: They involve an increased workload for personnel.
这些工作涉及增加人员工作量。
They are very tiring to put on.
The content can be weakened through financial pressure.
其内容可能因财政压力而被削弱。

points: 题干问“人们用来称呼/形容 blockbusters 的词语",第D段列举了多个词。
回到对应内容“此外，来访的公众已被称为顾客，而不是游客，博物馆重视的新客户通过大门的技能已经改变”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: …, it can be offered to other organizations for a fee.
连接词 once 引出“Once the museum that created the exhibition has shown it to its local market”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 once 把这一层关系补进去。
…, visitors thus lured are likely to stay longer at the museum.
连接词 while 引出“While partaking of the excitement of the blockbuster”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Museums in Australia, like other pleasure-giving public organizations, are adapting their activities so that they more closely reflect the marketplace.
澳大利亚的博物馆与其他娱乐性公共组织一样，正在调整其活动，以便更密切地反映市场。
